study.question: Does the small conditional click-AUC advantage of event-aligned membership through the primary population-normalization route require gradients through its population moments, or can native forward moments retain it when those derivatives are blocked?
study.hypothesis: Observed limitation: the native feedback model scores 0.668961270556 versus counts 0.668900839165 and permutation 0.668885292032; these tiny gaps are not uncertainty-qualified. Under uniform auxiliary readout, full/counts/permuted score 0.668889933412 / 0.668876485510 / 0.668816081748 (gaps +0.000013447902 and +0.000073851664). With row-local primary normalization and uniform auxiliary readout all three score exactly 0.667735412502; with row-local normalization and feedback readout full/counts/permuted score 0.667753698185 / 0.667695484679 / 0.667738095363. The existing row-local replacement changes both forward normalization and backward coupling and lowers overall quality by about 0.0012, so it cannot attribute the normalization route. The new hypothesis is that membership-dependent forward population moments may retain alignment utility without moment-mediated cotangents. Test it with native-forward, detached-moment normalization at uniform auxiliary readout. This is an exploratory controlled attribution question; no new accuracy, mechanism confirmation or novelty is asserted. Multiple trajectories caution against a universal assignment story: membership-blind fell to 0.668407891457, equal-mass full/counts reversed order (0.668860752933 / 0.668949130506), feedback-blocked full/counts both declined (0.668478673002 / 0.668392823990). Repeated native bridges returned identical AUC and establish reproducibility at one seed, not independent support. All visible trials succeeded; no previous execution error is present.

nearest_work.difference: Archived primary text, section 5.2 lines 317-335, defines Dice with minibatch moments during training and moving moments at test time. Inherit its target activation and distribution-adaptive gate; introduce only a diagnostic custom input Jacobian, retaining native gate values. Not an original DIN reproduction or priority claim.

Pinned Dice lines 25-34 uses non-affine BatchNorm1d, eps=1e-9, momentum=0.01 and learned alpha. Native-forward wrapper preserves that BN call, sigmoid and arithmetic order, changing only the normalized-input backward to g/sqrt(biased_var+eps) in detached cells.

Pinned benchmark implementation initializes task sequence hubs from task-specific masked averages (lines 133-139). This suite adds no hubs, projections or repeated broadcasts; it isolates use of existing mask-derived strata in the local scorer. Equivalence to the original INFNet paper remains unverified.
Only original-paper link and provenance are available from the registry; full original text was not supplied. No claim of paper reproduction or originality relative to it.

Inherit the complete standalone model and path controls. Add primary_moment_gradient=native|detached with unchanged forward normalization, instead of substituting within-row channel moments. Prior source digest ba7c0aadb6a18055bbd94aa99a72055cbf3e1d407ec27da4416f0f96be01f61d verified.

Read-only lines 383-408 derive task masks from historical action-vocabulary tokens. Preserve host masks and action codes; changes concern representation use of a redundant derived signal, not new information or host label construction.

inherited_components: Strongest visible g3-r0065 model and its exact learned capacity; all seven supplied ancestor-source SHA256 digests verified against workspace contract; candidate.py initially byte-identical to the incumbent.
g1-r0084 native-uniform standalone implementation, full/counts/permuted representations, joint-pattern-preserving valid-rank rotation, existing registered auxiliary normalization buffers.
DIN local-activation scorer, native Dice in towers, field embeddings, fixed target-match and ordinal summaries, residual adapters and context/history product fusion.
All incumbent context-cotangent collection, orientation and assignment functions and four-task supervision; this proposal does not intervene on the auxiliary objective or those transfer rules.
study.proposed_difference: At each primary training Dice, call the original BatchNorm once on the same expanded 70-row population, preserving native values and state updates. A custom autograd identity returns those normalized values exactly. Native mode routes its cotangent into the real BN graph. Detached mode routes g*rsqrt(Var_biased[X]+eps) directly into X and none into the BN graph, treating moments as constants. The inverse scale is computed without gradients in FP32 in all arms; Dice sigmoid, learned alpha, direct X edges and every eval operation stay native. Cross detached mode with full, counts-only and existing permuted membership, all at uniform auxiliary readout, plus a full native-uniform bridge. This is a controlled surrogate-backward diagnostic, not a wholly new unified architecture. The original strongest model remains the utility reference, not replaced as incumbent before measured validation.
predictions: Host prerequisite: at identical full-membership weights and buffers, bridge versus detached full must have identical training forward outputs and primary running buffers for each matched call; evaluation must be identical. Confirm state_dict keys, parameter counts/order, RNG state and checkpoint round trips. Use native FP32 and frozen BF16 autocast, without changing host training flags or labels.

Host derivative prerequisite: on synthetic finite preactivations the detached normalized-input Jacobian is diagonal in rows, matching a direct detached-mean/variance reference within FP32/BF16 tolerance. For a loss on uniform rows, nonuniform support cotangents must be zero in detached mode; native mode can retain nonzero support cotangents. Dice alpha and direct-X gradients remain live. Test empty history, singleton/mixed occupied blocks, zero/near-constant preactivations, duplicated support rows and partial validation batches.

Bridge should reproduce the native-uniform full reference 0.668889933412 to host reproducibility tolerance. Deviation or failed parity is execution/implementation evidence, not scientific counterevidence; do not interpret detached scores until resolved and count all costs.

If forward population moments suffice for conditional assignment utility, detached full should exceed both detached counts and detached permutation; report both AUC differences and compare their changes relative to native-uniform gaps +0.000013447902 and +0.000073851664. No positive direction is established by one tiny gap.

If moment-mediated cotangents are necessary in this implementation, both detached alignment gaps should shrink toward zero or reverse while the bridge remains intact. Large shared quality shifts or gradient amplification require an optimization follow-up before causal interpretation.

Report primary click AUC and unweighted Logloss, all four task metrics, auxiliary mean separately, inherited history-length slices with positive/negative counts, parameters, train/allocated GPU seconds, wall time, examples, peak memory, throughput and whole-batch p50/p95 latency. Analyze full-vs-counts and full-vs-permuted differences within each route; do not select on four-task mean.

For attribution record gradient RMS/norm and clipping rates plus recomputed-vs-native inverse-scale error where host diagnostics are available. Permutation must preserve each task count and joint-pattern multiset per valid ten-event block, leave padded entries zero and keep item/action values/order unchanged; mark unchanged/periodic blocks as nondiscriminating.

Any uncertainty estimate must use paired user-cluster bootstrap only if authorized user identity/grouping is available to host; do not invent IDs inside forward. Additional paired seeds require the host-authorized repetition interface; the present protocol seed is fixed and exact reruns are not seed variation.
falsifiers: Detached full failing to exceed either counts or permutation undermines sufficiency of forward-moment assignment utility in this controlled route; it does not refute mask utility in the native feedback model.
Detached full/counts equality combined with lower permuted performance supports avoiding a disruptive surrogate at most, not positive usefulness of original assignment beyond counts.

Persistence of both full-vs-control gaps after blocking moment derivatives undermines the claim that population-moment cotangents are necessary; it does not establish that moment values alone explain the original model.

Capacity, host inputs, gradient ownership, forward/state parity or synthetic derivative checks failing invalidates the intended comparison; a failed control must be retained and corrected within the budget.

A tiny one-seed gain without discriminating repetition and user-cluster uncertainty remains preliminary. Overall score degradation or cost growth can reject the implementation for utility even if an attribution signal remains.
alternative_explanations: These are surrogate gradients: removing population derivatives also changes gradient scale/geometry and optimization. It does not isolate one semantic membership bit or prove that native backward coupling alone is beneficial.

FP32 torch.var recomputation can differ from native BatchNorm saved inverse standard deviation under BF16. Quantify derivative-scale error against an independently detached-moment reference on the host before interpreting results.
Earlier references and this suite share one frozen seed. Exact reruns are reproducibility bridges, not independent mechanism replications; no seed change is allowed by this proposal.

One fixed half-valid-count rotation within each ten-event block preserves joint patterns, counts and coarse recency but is not a randomization distribution; singleton, constant-pattern and periodic blocks can be invariant.
Membership is a deterministic transform of supplied action codes in the inspected loader. The question is conditional representation/optimization utility, not additional statistical information.
Native bridge adds parameter-free diagnostic work; runtime is measured rather than assumed matched to older modules. Ordinary BF16 roundoff and GPU scheduling can affect tiny validation differences.
The seed-specific gaps may be rounding, optimization noise or validation selection rather than stable conditional utility.
Mask frequency and joint membership patterns rather than event content association can explain some benefit; counts-only and within-block joint permutation test different nulls.

Primary normalization, auxiliary readout and inherited context-cotangent transfer interact. Closing auxiliary grouped readout changes the scientific scope; findings cannot be transferred unconditionally to native feedback readout.
Whole-window vocabularies, static snapshots, official_offline delayed feedback and category/brand-based auxiliary attribution limit production interpretation.
